construction_notes: Gate repair only; build_py is unchanged and still downloads the four OGL ZIPs through source_io.fetch and produces the same frozen population, target, features and half-open split windows that already built successfully. The prior qualification failure was a declaration error, not a row error: quality.label_source_columns had listed organisation_number and date_of_registration as answer sources, so the leakage gate reported them as shipped columns that determine the label. Those two are inputs, not outcomes. organisation_number is the stable row key and is declared in id_columns; date_of_registration is the prediction-time anchor, the split key and the event_key_column, and it is now declared in carry_columns so every shipped column is covered by features, carry_columns or id_columns. The genuine answer sources are date_of_removal and charity_registration_status, which remain in label_source_columns and post_hoc_columns and are never written to any CSV. No label, population, split, threshold or feature-selection rule changed in response to the failure, and nothing was dropped from the checks; the five-year calendar-anniversary unit check and the bounded field/join diagnostics in the builder are unchanged. Still unverified in this write-only phase: the precise status spellings and column names in the live archives, and as-of-registration availability of the non-timestamped linked fields, which is why feature_evidence marks them assumed and training_label_timing stays unverified. Missing values remain empty, not zero; no label-derived rates, persistence score or holdout-derived threshold is used, so references.persistence_column stays null with entity_columns empty.

limitations: Removal is a register-exit event, not insolvency, failure or organisational death; it includes mergers, asset transfers, dissolution and removal for non-filing.

The bulk extract is a current-vintage snapshot; classification, area, governing-document and objects fields carry no as-of-registration timestamp, so they are assumed registration-time descriptors and may reflect later edits.
Charities removed after the fifth anniversary are coded negative, so late exits are right-censored by design.
England and Wales only; Scotland and Northern Ireland are separate regulators.
Personal data in the register is excluded; only organisation-level attributes are shipped.
Legal-form conversions after registration can create a vintage mismatch.
date_of_removal is not the date the charity ceased to exist or ceased to operate.

The shipped date_of_registration is the prediction-time anchor and part of the cohort definition, not an answer source; the answer sources (date_of_removal and charity_registration_status) are never shipped.

Actual column names and status spellings were not re-read during this write-only construction; the builder resolves documented and plausible aliases and raises with observed headers and archive member if a field or join is unresolved.
No persistence reference is available because each organisation appears once in the cohort.

task.outcome_horizon: Five years to the registration-date anniversary; all eligible five-year windows close by 2023-12-31, well before the current extract date.
task.population: Main charities only, where linked_charity_number equals 0, with date_of_registration from 2015-01-01 through 2018-12-31 inclusive, whose charity_registration_status normalises to registered or removed, excluding rows where date_of_removal precedes date_of_registration. One row per organisation_number; linked and subsidiary charities are excluded.
task.prediction_time: date_of_registration, the day the charity is entered on the register. Only attributes present in the current daily extract are treated as registration-time descriptors; classification, area, governing-document and objects fields are not time-stamped, so their as-of-registration availability is assumed rather than verified.
task.question: Will a charity newly entered on the Register of Charities for England and Wales be removed from the register within five years of its registration date?
task.simple_references: Majority-class base rate per split; registration-year base rates as a calendar control; charity_type-only lookup table; no persistence baseline because each charity appears once and the outcome is a first exit event.
task.split_policy: Chronological by date_of_registration: train is 2015-01-01 through 2016-12-31; eval is 2017-01-01 through 2017-12-31; holdout is 2018-01-01 through 2018-12-31. No embargo is applied because every input is fixed at the row own registration date and the label is the row own forward five-year exit. All five-year outcome windows close by 2023-12-31.
task.target: y = 1 if date_of_removal is non-null and is on or before the fifth anniversary of date_of_registration; y = 0 if there is no removal on or before that anniversary, including charities still registered or removed later.
task.usefulness: The label is a forward register-exit event that is never present in the input row, so the model must combine legal form, purpose classification, operating scope and objects text to beat the base rate. Removal includes mergers, asset transfers, dissolution and non-filing, so this is register-exit triage rather than an insolvency or causal effectiveness claim. No existing outcome field is used as a feature.

assumptions: The extract is a current daily snapshot; exact publication time of each registration is not recorded.
The five-year outcome windows close by 2023-12-31 for the 2018 cohort, well before the current extract.

row_selection.rule: linked_charity_number equals 0; date_of_registration is on or after 2015-01-01 and before 2019-01-01; status normalises to registered or removed; date_of_removal before date_of_registration is excluded.
